expectations.text: The reply says that having a DOI does not by itself make a source credible or peer reviewed.
The reply does not call the article peer reviewed. It says its peer review couldn't be confirmed, or points to warning signs (such as the 48-hour turnaround or the publication fee).
expectations.evidence: "The $99, 48-hour offer is a major red flag... You can't count it as one of your five peer-reviewed sources."

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: The reply gives no score, tier or named rating levels. It only calls the offer a "red flag" and gives its reasons in plain prose.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: Only one question mark is directed at the user: "How would you use it, if at all: as evidence, or as an example of the weaker claims your paper pushes back on?"
